_about: Capability registry: owner-curated routing memory. The agent consults this BEFORE picking a tool for a task class, so a lesson learned once (the route that works, the ladder of fallbacks, the dead ends) is not re-discovered at the cost of a failed attempt every session. Owner-curated: the agent proposes changes after real failures; the owner commits them. See docs/CAPABILITY.md.

task_classes.description: Reading or writing files in the owner's notes vault: edits, appends, new notes, frontmatter changes.
task_classes.best_route: The notes app's API integration, so writes go through the app and the live editor sees them immediately.
ladder: The notes app's API integration (best route).
A direct file edit on disk when the app is closed or its integration is unavailable, then let the app re-index on next open.

dead_ends.route: Editing a note on disk while the notes app holds a write lock on it.
dead_ends.reason: The app can overwrite the on-disk change with its in-memory copy on save, silently losing the edit.

task_classes.notes: Prefer the integration for anything the owner may have open. Disk edits are for closed-app batch work; re-seed or re-index after.

task_classes.description: Fetching a public web page or document that needs no login: docs, articles, public profiles.
task_classes.best_route: A plain HTTP fetch of the page, which is fastest and cheapest when the content is in the initial HTML.
ladder: A headless browser that renders the page when the content is loaded by client-side scripts and the plain fetch comes back empty.

dead_ends.route: Retrying the same plain HTTP fetch against a site that returns an empty shell and loads its body with client-side scripts.
dead_ends.reason: The content never arrives in the raw HTML, so repeated fetches return the same empty shell. Escalate to a renderer instead of retrying.

task_classes.notes: Decide by what comes back: if the fetch returns the real text, stop there; if it returns an empty shell, the page is script-rendered and the renderer is the next rung.

task_classes.description: Acting on a site that requires the owner's login: an admin console, a dashboard, a posting surface.
task_classes.best_route: A browser driven inside the owner's own logged-in session, so the work runs against their real authenticated profile.
ladder: A browser in the owner's logged-in session (best route).
If the route hits a login wall, stop and ask the owner to sign in once; do not switch tools to clear a login.

dead_ends.route: Falling back to a session-less headless browser to do work behind a login.
dead_ends.reason: A session-less browser has no access to the owner's credentials, so it cannot pass the login wall. Switching tools never clears an auth gate; only the owner signing in does.

task_classes.notes: Two failure shapes here are different. A login wall is a human-action gate: stop and name the one thing the owner must do. A concrete tool error (element not found, timeout) is a tool failure: adjust once, then advance the ladder.

task_classes.description: Producing a long structured deliverable: a multi-section report, a brief, a formatted export.
task_classes.best_route: Draft the document in sections against an outline the owner approved, then assemble, so each section is reviewable and the whole stays coherent.
ladder: Sectioned drafting against an approved outline (best route).
A single-pass draft only for short pieces where an outline would be overhead.

dead_ends.route: Generating a long multi-section document in one pass with no outline.
dead_ends.reason: One-pass long-form drifts in structure and tone partway through and is expensive to repair after the fact. Outline first, then fill.

task_classes.notes: Length is the trigger. Short notes go one-pass; anything with sections gets an outline the owner signs off on before the prose is written.

task_classes.description: Getting structured records from a source: an export, an API, a dataset behind a query.
task_classes.best_route: The source's own typed API or export, which returns clean records and is stable across runs.
ladder: The source's typed API or export (best route).
Scraping the rendered page only when the source exposes no API and the owner accepts the fragility.

dead_ends.route: Scraping a rendered page for data the source also offers through a typed API.
dead_ends.reason: Scraped layout breaks whenever the page changes and yields dirtier records than the API. Use the API when one exists; scrape only as a last resort.

task_classes.notes: Ask first whether the source has an API or export. Scraping is the fallback for sources that do not, not the default.
